Class Variables, Variable-Name Variables, Class Expression Variables & Type Variables

How to Understand It

Core Ontological & Syntactic Rules for Variables (See FACTBOOK.md):

  • Classes Cannot Be Free or Bound: A Class is a semantic collection, not a syntactic variable. Only variables have binder occurrences (at the binding site {x | 𝛗}, ∀(x:Class)𝛗, let x = t in 𝛗, displayed in yellow with tooltip ending in (binder)), bound occurrences (inside the scope of a binder, displayed in yellow), or free occurrences (displayed in red).
  • Strict Sort Distinction: Obelisk distinguishes variable (Variable/Name), class (Class), class variable (x : Class), variable-name variable (v : Variable / x : Name), class expression variable (k, t : Class.Expression), formula variable (𝛗 : Fm), and type variable (A, X : Type).
  • Class Variables (x, y, z, u, w, A, B, C, K, Q, X, Y, Z : Class): By default, object variables range over Class. Whether a class x is a set is expressed by the predicate (x set) (Entry DefIsSet (3.02)), never by changing its type away from Class.
  • Subscripted Dependent-Branch Variables (Tₑ, t₁, t₂): Used in Entry DefSimpleConditional (3.23) and Entry DefDependentConditional (3.24) (if_dep) for the target type family Tₑ and the true/false branch witnesses t₁ and t₂.
Canonical Law (Unicode)
∀(x:Class). ∀(Y:Class). ((x ∈ Y) ⇒ (x set))
